column6: The team explains, with named examples, what worked, what did not, and what it would do differently, and the handoff reflects it.
column9: General lessons with few specifics; the handoff does not show them.
column12: No lessons the team can articulate.

column6: Requirements are complete, prioritized, and current; what shipped matches them, or the difference was negotiated with the partner.
column9: Requirements are mostly documented; there is drift between the document and what shipped.
column12: Requirements are missing or stale; the delivered work does not map to them.

column6: Deployed where it needs to run, documented for its successor, used by the partner or their users, and no gap the partner raised remains open.
column9: Deployed and functional, with gaps the team has named and not yet closed.
column12: Not deployed, or deployed but unusable without the team present.

column5: People outside the team depend on it (full points)
column6: Consultancy: the partner runs it in operations. FOSS: patches shipped in an upstream release. Research: a stranger reproduced the result from the published artifact. New Product or Game: sustained use by strangers (tens of heavy or hundreds of light users).
column8: Someone outside the team runs it in their own environment (90% of the points)
column9: Consultancy: the partner is integrating it into production. FOSS: patches merged. Research: a person outside the team reran the pipeline on real data and got the numbers. New Product or Game: two dozen strangers used it.
column11: An outsider ran it and the team acted on what they found (80% of the points)
column12: Consultancy: the partner's feedback on a prototype addressed in a newer version. FOSS: a pull request reviewed and revised. Research: the partner's group ran it on real data and the issues were fixed. New Product or Game: a dozen strangers, or a completed user study.
column14: An outsider ran it once (70% of the points)
column15: Consultancy: the partner tried a prototype. FOSS: a pull request submitted. Research: a real-data run shown to the partner. New Product or Game: friends tried a deployed build.
column17: The partner watched it run on their real inputs (60% of the points)
column18: A live demo or a recording, but nobody outside the team has operated it.
column20: Nobody outside the team has run it (half the points)

column6: Whole team present and prepared; anyone can speak to the project; disagreements are resolved and reported to the partner; work is visibly spread across members.
column9: Mostly present; one or two members carry the meetings; disagreements show in a meeting and are settled by the next one.
column12: Members missing without notice; one person does the talking and the work; conflict visible and unmanaged.

column6: Agenda before, every voice during, notes after, working demos, and updates on cadence, every time.
column9: Meetings are prepared and followed up most of the time; one or two students rarely speak; the partner occasionally has to chase an update.
column12: Meetings without an agenda or notes; the same one or two people speak; the partner chases for updates; demos are slides.
